name: Jodey C. Arrington

data_centers.summary: Arrington is one of the loudest boosters of the AI data center buildout in Congress. He hosted the September 2025 launch of OpenAI's Stargate campus in Abilene, calls West Texas the 'Silicon Prairie,' and in May 2026 sat on a Reagan Economic Forum panel on AI infrastructure that covered permitting and regulatory reform. No statements found raising concerns about ratepayers, water or housing costs.

evidence.title: Press release: Arrington touts Stargate's $100 billion Abilene investment ('Shackleford vs Shanghai, Big Country vs Beijing')
evidence.quote: From construction jobs to cutting-edge careers, this project means opportunities for our people, billions in private investment, and a powerful reminder that America - not China - will lead in the technologies of tomorrow.
evidence.what_it_shows: He celebrates the largest AI data center project in the country in his own district and frames it as jobs and beating China.

evidence.title: KTXS: Political leaders and investors tour Abilene's Project Stargate
evidence.quote: There's no better place to build the backbone for AI than West Texas because of our abundant and reliable energy, our workforce, our hard-working, God fearing, freedom-loving people
evidence.what_it_shows: At the Stargate tour with Sam Altman and Sen. Cruz he pitched West Texas as the ideal place to build more AI compute.

evidence.title: C-SPAN: Rep. Jodey Arrington and policy stakeholders on AI infrastructure and energy needs (Reagan Economic Forum, Simi Valley)
evidence.what_it_shows: C-SPAN's program summary says the panel covered data centers, competition with China, permitting and regulatory reform, and grid concerns; he appeared as the buildout-friendly congressional voice.

ai_risk.summary: Arrington talks about AI as a race with China that America must win and as a force for good; he has not called for safety rules on AI models. No statement found on catastrophic AI risk, chatbots or deepfakes, so this score rests on his innovation-first framing only.

evidence.title: KTXS: Arrington at the Stargate tour on the AI race
evidence.quote: we're the new frontier for information technology and in support of the AI race for our great country
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames AI as a national race to win, and KTXS reports he believes AI can be a powerful force for good; no mention of guardrails.

evidence.title: Press release: Arrington touts new AI investments in West Texas
evidence.quote: America - not China - will lead in the technologies of tomorrow.
evidence.what_it_shows: His AI message is about American leadership over China rather than about risks or regulation.

tech_regulation.summary: The only tech rule he has backed is the Connected Vehicle Security Act, which bans internet-connected cars and parts from companies tied to China, Russia, Iran or North Korea. That is a national security measure, not a Big Tech stance. No position found on Section 230, antitrust or kids online safety.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 8730, Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a ban on connected cars and car software from companies tied to foreign adversaries, a targeted tech restriction with 80 cosponsors.

preemption.summary: No public statement found on whether Washington should override state AI laws. Searched for his reaction to the 2025 moratorium in H.R. 1 (which he shepherded as Budget chairman), the December 2025 executive order and the March 2026 White House framework, and found nothing.

china_chips.summary: No statement or bill found on AI chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China as of September 2026. His 'America not China' language is about building compute at home, not about chip exports.

signature: House Budget chairman and West Texas booster of OpenAI's Stargate campus in Abilene who brands the region the 'Silicon Prairie' and frames the AI buildout as beating China; retiring in January 2027.

notable_quote.text: From construction jobs to cutting-edge careers, this project means opportunities for our people, billions in private investment, and a powerful reminder that America - not China - will lead in the technologies of tomorrow.

groups: House Committee on the Budget, Chairman (119th Congress)
search_notes: Ran about 12 Google News queries (AI, data centers/Stargate, chips/export controls, preemption/moratorium, Big Tech/Section 230, Abilene housing backlash, Abbott's pause, Reagan Forum, Byrd Bot, Ways and Means AI) plus his press release listing. Wayback-based site listing was down (503). Opened and confirmed the Stargate release, the KTXS tour story and the C-SPAN program page (description only, no transcript). Also found H.R. 9892 Stop EU Overreach Act (July 2026), framed around energy producers, not tech, so not scored. Announced retirement November 2025. Not on the Leading the Future endorsement lists checked.

name: Joaquin Castro

data_centers.summary: No public statements found on data centers as of September 2026, including on San Antonio projects, ratepayer bills or Abbott's 2026 interconnection pause.

ai_risk.summary: Castro signed two August 2026 House Democratic letters: one telling Speaker Johnson that Congress has failed to respond to AI threats and demanding AI CEOs testify under oath, and one to OpenAI with 23 questions about a security incident and whether its models tried to undermine human control. He has not sponsored binding AI safety legislation himself.

evidence.title: Casar-led letter from 20 House Democrats demanding congressional hearings with AI CEOs under oath (Castro signer)
evidence.quote: The CEOs of the largest AI companies should answer questions under oath, and Americans should have a chance to hear from independent experts on the dangers posed by this technology.
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined a call that treats AI development as a safety threat and a job-displacement threat that Congress has failed to address.

evidence.title: Casar and Matsui letter to OpenAI on its security incident and misalignment safeguards (Castro signer)
evidence.quote: whether any model has taken actions to undermine OpenAI’s ability to control, align, or oversee future models
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants answers from a frontier lab about loss-of-control risks, a transparency and oversight posture.

tech_regulation.summary: Castro backs targeted rules: he cosponsored two 2026 kids online safety bills and the My Body, My Data Act protecting reproductive health data from apps and data brokers. No position found on Section 230 repeal or breaking up Big Tech.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 6289, Promoting a Safe Internet for Minors Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports new federal work to make the internet safer for children.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 6499, Assessing Safety Tools for Parents and Minors Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a government study of parental control tools, a modest kids-safety step.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 3420, My Body, My Data Act of 2023 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed a major privacy bill limiting how apps and companies collect and share reproductive health data.

preemption.summary: No position found. He did not sign the November 2025 Matsui letter (81 House Democrats) or the December 2025 Clarke letter (44 signers) against a federal moratorium on state AI laws; both signer lists were checked. No statement found on the December 2025 executive order or the March 2026 White House framework.

china_chips.summary: Castro is a China chip hawk. He was an original cosponsor of the RESTRICT Act, which would bar sales of Nvidia H200 and other advanced AI chips to China after President Trump allowed them, and he co-led a bill giving the government ten years instead of five to punish export control violations.

evidence.title: Original cosponsor: H.R. 6879, RESTRICT Act (Restoring Export and Security Trade Restrictions for Integrated Circuit Technologies Act)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs a ban on selling the most advanced AI chips, including the H200, to China and other countries of concern.

evidence.title: House Foreign Affairs Democrats press release: Meeks introduces bill to block sales of advanced AI chips to China (lists Castro as original cosponsor)
evidence.quote: Prohibits the sale of H200 and other advanced AI chips to China.
evidence.what_it_shows: The committee release names Castro among the original cosponsors of a bill written to reverse the Trump decision to sell H200s to China.

evidence.title: Cosponsor and Democratic co-lead: H.R. 8202, ten-year statute of limitations for export control violations
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants more time to prosecute companies that illegally export controlled technology.

evidence.title: Nextgov: Tech bills of the week, boosting export controls (Mackenzie and Castro bill)
evidence.quote: would increase the statute of limitations for export control violations from five years to 10 years
evidence.what_it_shows: Reporting confirms Castro co-led the bipartisan export control enforcement bill with Rep. Ryan Mackenzie.

signature: House Foreign Affairs and Intelligence Democrat who is a China chip hawk (original cosponsor of the RESTRICT Act to block H200 sales) and who signed the August 2026 letters demanding AI CEOs testify under oath.

notable_quote.text: The CEOs of the largest AI companies should answer questions under oath, and Americans should have a chance to hear from independent experts on the dangers posed by this technology.

search_notes: Ran about 12 Google News queries (AI, data centers, chips/export controls, surveillance AI, Big Tech/Section 230/TikTok, preemption/OpenAI, San Antonio data centers, Spanish-language misinformation, national security AI, kids online safety, AI super PACs, deepfakes). His 2026 coverage is dominated by ICE detention work; almost nothing on AI in his own press releases. Confirmed both Casar letters list him as a signer, confirmed RESTRICT Act cosponsorship on the HFAC Democrats release and its bill number (H.R. 6879) via GovTrack, and confirmed he is not on the Matsui letter PDF or Clarke letter. No AI super PAC support or attacks found.

name: Chip Roy

data_centers.summary: Roy is a conservative skeptic of the data center boom. He calls data centers 'massive sucks on power,' says homes, hospitals and businesses should come before them, wants them to supply their own water and power, and in May 2026 filed the POWER Act requiring the Energy Department to report how much water and energy data centers use. He has not called for a moratorium.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R. 9019, Public Oversight of Water and Energy Reporting (POWER) Act
evidence.what_it_shows: His own bill would force federal reporting of data center water and energy consumption.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Roy introduces POWER Act to increase transparency on data center water and energy use
evidence.quote: States like Texas have been enduring extreme drought conditions, and as we build out energy intensive data center infrastructure, we must have a clear picture of how much water and energy these projects are consuming.
evidence.what_it_shows: He ties the buildout to Texas drought and demands an honest accounting before more projects are built.

evidence.title: KLTV: Rep. Chip Roy raises questions over data centers as he campaigns for attorney general
evidence.quote: We need to know that we’re going to have the ability to sustain these things when we get them created and developed.
evidence.what_it_shows: He called data centers 'massive sucks on power,' said homes and hospitals should come first, and doubted that current contracts hold companies accountable for their water use.

ai_risk.summary: No scored position. Google News lists an August 24, 2026 Fox Business segment titled 'There needs to be a serious conversation in Washington about AI: Rep Chip Roy,' but the clip could not be opened, so no quote or score is recorded. No bills, letters or statements on AI safety, chatbots or deepfakes were found.

tech_regulation.summary: The only tech measure on his record is cosponsoring the 2024 bill forcing TikTok's Chinese owner to sell or face a ban. No position found on Section 230 reform, antitrust or kids online safety bills, so this is a thin, low-confidence read.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 7521, Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed forcing a sale or ban of TikTok, a targeted restriction on a foreign-controlled platform.

preemption.summary: No statement found on federal preemption of state AI laws, the 2025 moratorium in H.R. 1, the December 2025 executive order or the March 2026 White House framework, despite searches aimed at Freedom Caucus reaction to the moratorium.

china_chips.summary: No statement or bill found on AI chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China. His China-related bills in 2026 concern visas for Chinese nationals, not chips.

signature: Freedom Caucus conservative and 2026 Texas attorney general candidate who filed the POWER Act to track data center water and energy use and calls data centers 'massive sucks on power'; not seeking re-election to the House.

notable_quote.text: As data centers spring up across the country, we need to be mindful of our water and energy resources.

search_notes: Ran about 11 Google News queries (AI, data centers, Big Tech/Section 230/antitrust, moratorium/preemption, AI risk keywords, chips/export controls, Fox Business AI segment, kids/chatbots, AG candidate Q&As, Politico AI regulation piece) and read his press release and In the News listings. Confirmed the POWER Act release and quotes on roy.house.gov and the bill number (H.R. 9019) via GovTrack; confirmed the KLTV interview quotes. Google News URL decoding hit rate limits, so the Aug 24, 2026 Fox Business clip, a Sept 10, 2026 Politico piece and two Texas Tribune AG Q&As could not be opened. The state context file's note placing him on the E&C Privacy Working Group and at an E&C FERC hearing appears misattributed (he sits on Judiciary, Rules and Budget) and was not used. He voted no on the FY27 NDAA (H.R. 8800) citing its cost, not AI provisions.

name: Troy E. Nehls

data_centers.summary: No public position found on building data centers, ratepayer protections or Abbott's 2026 pause. His November 2025 op-ed discusses data center hardware security, not whether or where to build them.

ai_risk.summary: Nehls frames AI as a race the United States must win and backs faster AI deployment: a November 2025 op-ed on securing AI infrastructure, a March 2026 letter praising the Energy Department's Genesis Mission to deploy AI in science, and cosponsorship of a bill funding university AI research for the military. No statements found calling for safety rules on AI models.

evidence.title: Op-ed in the Washington Reporter (posted on nehls.house.gov): To win the global AI race, we must secure our optical transceivers and prioritize American-made components
evidence.quote: Protecting our AI infrastructure is critical to winning the global AI race.
evidence.what_it_shows: His AI agenda is about winning the race and hardening infrastructure, not about limits on AI development.

evidence.title: Washington Reporter: Lawmakers laud Trump administration's AI Genesis Mission (Nehls signed Gooden letter to Energy Secretary Wright)
evidence.quote: landmark effort to deploy Artificial Intelligence (AI) to revolutionize American scientific productivity
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined House Republicans applauding a federal push to deploy AI faster across national labs.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 5466, GUARD Act (university AI research for the military)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports federal money for AI research tied to defense needs.

tech_regulation.summary: Nehls backs targeted rules on platforms from a conservative angle: he cosponsors the Stop the Censorship Act to strip Section 230 protection when platforms remove lawful speech, the STOP CSAM Act to make platforms liable for child abuse material, and the SHIELD Act to criminalize sharing intimate images without consent. He has not called for breaking up Big Tech.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 908, Stop the Censorship Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would let people sue social media companies that remove posts they merely find objectionable, narrowing Section 230.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 3921, STOP CSAM Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports new duties and liability for platforms over child sexual abuse material.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 1218, SHIELD Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a federal crime for sharing private intimate images without consent; he also cosponsored the 2023 and 2024 versions (H.R. 3686, H.R. 10329).

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 5182, Child Online Safety Modernization Act of 2023 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed fuller reporting of child abuse material by online companies in the prior Congress.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 4791, Free Speech Protection Act (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would bar officials from pressuring platforms to take down posts; shows his platform concerns center on censorship.

preemption.summary: No statement found on federal preemption of state AI laws, the 2025 moratorium, the December 2025 executive order or the March 2026 White House framework.

china_chips.summary: Nehls is a China tech hawk on supply chains rather than on chip exports. His op-ed warns that Chinese-made optical transceivers in AI data centers could carry hidden firmware and calls for American-made components, and his PROTECT Act would penalize universities that sell research rights to China. No position found on Nvidia H20/H200 sales or the Chip Security Act.

evidence.title: Op-ed: To win the global AI race, we must secure our optical transceivers and prioritize American-made components
evidence.quote: Foreign adversaries, such as China, can insert malicious firmware or hidden surveillance tools into transceivers, potentially corrupting our networks.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants Chinese-made networking parts kept out of American AI infrastructure and secured NDAA report language on the threat.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Troy E. Nehls introduces the PROTECT Act of 2026
evidence.quote: would prohibit U.S. universities from selling the intellectual property (IP) rights of research conducted by the university, their staff, or students to the government of a hostile nation, like China, Russia, or Iran
evidence.what_it_shows: Shows a hawkish posture on technology transfer to China, adjacent to but distinct from chip export controls.

signature: Retiring Judiciary and Transportation Republican whose AI focus is supply-chain security: a 2025 op-ed on keeping Chinese-made optical transceivers out of AI data centers, plus cosponsorship of Section 230 censorship and child-safety bills.

notable_quote.text: Foreign adversaries, such as China, can insert malicious firmware or hidden surveillance tools into transceivers, potentially corrupting our networks.

search_notes: Ran about 10 Google News queries (AI, data centers, Washington Reporter op-ed, Genesis Mission, Big Tech/Section 230/chatbots/deepfakes, chips/export controls/preemption/TikTok, AI in policing and transport, Section 230 and kids bills, NDAA AI) and read six pages of his press release listing. Confirmed the op-ed text on nehls.house.gov, the PROTECT Act release, and the Genesis Mission letter in the Washington Reporter article. Wayback-based site listing timed out. Announced retirement November 2025 (Trump endorsed his twin brother Trever to succeed him). Not on the Leading the Future endorsement lists checked; no AI super PAC activity found.
